NextItemRules: Oracle rows are the strongest naming route: the 6.4 released surface names them and a literal in the 6.3 body must corroborate the row.
A NewName may not repeat inside one type; the sibling stays open rather than taking a numeric suffix.
Virtual rows, interface implementations and contract-family members are renamed as a family.
One block is one review file, one --wave run, one checkpoint, one commit.

Codes: same-module name collision where the sibling has no distinct evidence
no-evidence-in-scope: every evidence route closed with a measured number (private state with no observable behaviour, no literal, no anchor, no readable counterpart)
HardBlockers.Rule: A turn may stop with work left only when every remaining row of the current block carries one of these codes, recorded with its token. While an unmeasured route remains, switch route instead.

Closure.Rule: The pass closes when every in-scope definition is exactly one of named | already-readable | SDK/protected | compiler-generated (merged) | unresolved-no-evidence with a reason, and Phase 4 has run.
Closure.Authority: GOAL.md task 5 and POLICY.md; the mission text allows unresolved rows explicitly and forbids claiming more than the evidence shows.
Closure.NotClaimed: Closing the naming phase is not a renamed or verified ETS; AppliedToSource stays false until Phase 4.

MemoryBlowup.RootCause: dnSpy 863effcee: a RECURSIVE lambda (a handler that subscribes itself - Knx.Ets.Common arx/b::c and UserControls ContextMenuPlacementBehavior/<>c__DisplayClass2_0::method_0). Inlining copies the body into its own body, so the AST grows without bound. Fixed by IsInLambdaCycle (walks the lambda's ldftn targets, memoized) plus relaxed backstop caps.
MemoryBlowup.Found: 2026-09-27: with '--no-anon-methods' the same module exported in 40 s at 3 GB, so lambda inlining is the trigger - it copies each lambda's AST into its call site and generated code creates hundreds per method.
MemoryBlowup.Fix: dnSpy 0bec3dd2f: a lambda above 400 IL instructions stays a method (DNSPY_MAX_INLINED_LAMBDA_IL) and each method accepts at most 2000 inlined IL instructions (DNSPY_MAX_INLINED_LAMBDA_IL_PER_METHOD). Readability is unchanged - HawkNET eh still shows its 13 lambdas and 31 awaits.
MemoryBlowup.Result: Knx.Ets.Ui.UserControls exports in ~40 s at ~3 GB (was >20 GB); the whole 64-module set exports in one process in 5.3 min at 7.1 GB.
MemoryBlowup.FinalExport: D:\knx_analysis\ets63-source-v381-final (64 projects, 13,296 .cs, ~5 min). Solution build: 14 errors left - Knx.Falcon 14 (CS7014 attribute placement, CS1061 member lookups) and Knx.Ets.Common.2 2 (CS1503). Those two categories are the next decompiler-output work.
